filter_applied: visual potential + actionable + at least one panel persona said it would change a decision

tier_1_flagship_candidates.headline: The K% Sell Window
tier_1_flagship_candidates.what_it_uncovers: Companion to the published K-trajectory piece, inverted to the seller's POV. Identifies the exact pre-trade season profile that maximizes return on a pitcher sale — and the orgs that systematically miss it.
tier_1_flagship_candidates.why_now: Three of four GM personas demanded seller-side framing. The K-trajectory article was the highest-rated piece on the site (mean 8.0). Inverting it is the single highest-yield article on the pipeline.
tier_1_flagship_candidates.evidence_status: Already in the data — Q4 quartile means already computed. Need to add sell-side aggregates by seller-team identity to identify which orgs sell late.
visuals: Quartile bar showing pre-trade K% trend × FV return per WAR shipped
Per-org scatter: how often each team's pitcher trades land in Q4 (the optimal sell window)
Calendar heatmap: which months produce the most Q4 sales
tier_1_flagship_candidates.actionability: A rebuilder reads this and knows the optimal months and pitcher profiles to maximize FV haul. A contender reads this and knows what the seller knows about their target.

tier_1_flagship_candidates.headline: The Pitching Coach Is the Edge
tier_1_flagship_candidates.what_it_uncovers: When you decompose the 'org dev fit' GM-edge signal further, how much of it is the pitching coach's identity vs the rest of the staff? Public coaches data exists in our DB; nobody has wired it to trade outcomes.
tier_1_flagship_candidates.why_now: Old-school veteran flagged this as the single biggest missing covariate ('drives more of the org dev fit effect than the GM does'). Mid-market wants it for similar reasons.
tier_1_flagship_candidates.evidence_status: Personnel agent in earlier sweep already pulled per-coach FIP deltas: range −2.01 (Marin) to +1.65 (Stottlemyre Jr.), but ANOVA p=0.74 across 33 coaches. The story is in the partial-pooling Bayesian model the agent flagged but didn't run.
visuals: Horizontal bar of pitching coaches ranked by acquired-pitcher FIP delta (with credibility intervals from Bayesian partial pooling)
Coach × org dev fit heatmap — does the coach drive the dev fit feature or vice versa
Time series: when a coach changes teams, what happens to the new org's acquired-pitcher outcomes
tier_1_flagship_candidates.actionability: Reframes 'we should trade for org X' to 'we should trade for coach Y at org X.' Could materially change which trade partners get prioritized.
tier_1_flagship_candidates.panel_demand: explicit from old-school, implicit from mid-market

tier_1_flagship_candidates.headline: Where Your Prospects Go to Win
tier_1_flagship_candidates.what_it_uncovers: Mirror of the org-fit hitter laboratory but seller-side. When a rebuilder ships a 50 FV prospect, the destination org's dev infrastructure predicts how much value they're leaving on the table.
tier_1_flagship_candidates.why_now: Rebuild persona's top request. Inverts a finding (org dev fit predicts acquired-player improvement) into a seller's decision tool (which destinations will most appreciate my outgoing prospects).
tier_1_flagship_candidates.evidence_status: Need to: compute per-(destination_org, FV_grade) MLB WAR delta on shipped prospects. Org dev fit features already exist; this just reorients them.
visuals: 30-team matrix: rows = sending org, cols = receiving org, cells = mean WAR delta of shipped prospects
Scatter: destination org dev fit vs realized prospect MLB-WAR over 3 years
Per-FV-grade bar: how much surplus a 45 / 50 / 55 / 60 FV prospect typically captures by destination tier
tier_1_flagship_candidates.actionability: Direct rebuilder use case — 'don't ship to org X if you can get the same package from org Y, because your prospect will appreciate 40% more at Y.'

tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.headline: The August Trap
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.what_it_uncovers: Post-deadline waiver-era pitching pickups produce FIP +0.55, xFIP +0.51, SIERA +0.57 — roughly 2× the deadline-window penalty and 3× offseason.
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.why_now: One of the cleanest seasonal signals in the dataset. n=342. Adverse selection mechanism is the actionable framing.
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.evidence_status: Fully evidenced from earlier timing agent sweep.
visuals: Calendar phase × FIP/xFIP/SIERA grouped bar
Per-pitcher scatter: prior-season FIP vs post-acquisition FIP, color-coded by acquisition month
Adverse selection chart: # teams that passed on a pitcher before final acquirer
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.actionability: Discount any August pitcher acquisition by ~half a run of expected ERA. Mid-market and big-market both said yes.

tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.headline: The 33-Point Swing: Where Young Hitters Become Players
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.what_it_uncovers: Age-advantaged MiLB hitters acquired by top hitter-dev orgs gain +16 wRC+. Same archetype at low-dev orgs: −17 wRC+. 33-point swing on identical talent.
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.why_now: Strongest interaction effect in the archetype agent's sweep. n=419. Replicates across two org-fit metrics independently.
visuals: 2×2 grid: hitter age advantage × org dev tier, with wRC+ delta in each cell
Org-level scatter: hitter dev fit vs realized wRC+ improvement on age-advantaged acquisitions
Per-org bar of 'hitter laboratory rating' — which orgs are the actual laboratories
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.actionability: Concrete trade-partner ranking for any rebuilder shipping young hitters and any contender buying them.

tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.headline: The Playoff Math Is Different — and Most Models Get It Wrong
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.what_it_uncovers: Reruns the V3 model with playoff-probability-delta × playoff-revenue as the outcome variable, not regular-season dollar surplus. The leaderboard of who's actually winning trades shifts substantially when you change the objective.
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.why_now: Big-market persona's #1 request. Receiver-side dollar surplus net-of-cost is structurally wrong for high-payroll teams. This article fixes the math and shows who actually wins under the right objective.
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.evidence_status: Need to compute. Playoff probability data exists in team_season_stats; need a model layer on top.
visuals: Side-by-side: GM leaderboard under dollar surplus vs leaderboard under playoff leverage
Per-trade scatter: dollar surplus vs playoff-leverage surplus — which trades flip sign
Top 10 'most playoff-leveraged trades of the last decade'
tier_2_strong_supporting_candidates.actionability: Big-market teams get a model that matches their objective function. Mid-market readers see whether their team's deadline buys are actually contributing to October.

tier_3_smaller_pieces.headline: The Career-Stage Sweet Spot
tier_3_smaller_pieces.what_it_uncovers: Age 28-30 acquisitions produce $8.4M dollar surplus per trade and 0.90 WAR — substantially more than 31+ ($4.1M, 0.30 WAR) and more than <25 (despite the youth premium). Market overprices 31+, underprices 28-30.
visuals: Age bucket bar chart (5 buckets × 3 outcomes)
Per-player scatter colored by age band

tier_3_smaller_pieces.headline: What FanGraphs Knows — and What It Doesn't
tier_3_smaller_pieces.what_it_uncovers: Recomputes the GM Edge Decomposition restricted to the subset of trades that actually include a graded prospect, addressing the panel's universal complaint that max_fv=0 was hiding a coverage problem behind a 'prospects don't matter' headline.
tier_3_smaller_pieces.why_now: Both mid-market and big-market personas flagged the original article's max_fv=0 instrument failure. A direct response builds credibility.
tier_3_smaller_pieces.evidence_status: Need to filter to trades with non-zero max_fv (~25% of sample) and recompute.
visuals: Side-by-side: original correlations vs prospect-included-only correlations
Per-FV-grade scatter: max FV vs realized prospect WAR delta
tier_3_smaller_pieces.actionability: Honest test of whether 'prospects don't matter' survives the restriction. May reverse the headline.

tier_3_smaller_pieces.headline: Dev Orgs Aren't What You Think They Are
tier_3_smaller_pieces.what_it_uncovers: High-track-record hitter-dev orgs improve slow bats by 9 xwOBA points. They erode high-barrel power hitters by 17 wRC+. The 'dev org' brand is a contact-and-discipline factory, not a power factory.
tier_3_smaller_pieces.why_now: Counter-intuitive reframing. Pairs naturally with #5 as a follow-up.
visuals: Archetype × org-tier 2×2 with wRC+ deltas
Per-org 'identity' bar — contact lab vs power lab
tier_3_smaller_pieces.actionability: Don't ship power hitters to contact-focused dev orgs. Don't pay dev-org premium for power acquisitions.

tier_4_infrastructure_not_articles.title: V3 model calibration page
tier_4_infrastructure_not_articles.what_it_is: Standing diagnostics page (not an article) — coverage, CRPS, residuals by trade archetype, calibration plots. Updates with each model refresh.
tier_4_infrastructure_not_articles.why_now: Top demand across personas. Mid-market said 'every downstream finding inherits this and I haven't seen it.' Build credibility for everything else.
tier_4_infrastructure_not_articles.deliverable: New route /research/model — separate from articles index. Three or four diagnostic charts, methodology prose.
